evals.prompt: Review this diff for my PR that adds a discount calculation to the cart.
evals.expected_output: Reads the change and surrounding context, then reports findings anchored to file:line and rated Must/Should/Consider with concrete fixes, prioritizing correctness (edge cases like empty cart, negative/zero, rounding, off-by-one) over style. Notes genuine strengths under Good. Does not rewrite the whole change.

evals.prompt: def get(u): d=db.q(u); return d[0]  — review this.
evals.expected_output: Flags correctness risks first (empty result -> index error on d[0], no not-found handling), then naming (get/u/d are vague), and missing error handling — each with a concrete fix. Severity-ordered with the correctness bug as Must fix.

evals.prompt: Review this — does it look okay?  try: charge(card) except: pass
evals.expected_output: Identifies the silent exception swallow as a Must-fix: failures are hidden, payment errors are ignored. Recommends handling or propagating with context and narrowing the except. Does not treat it as merely a style nit.

evals.prompt: Can you review my code? Mostly I want to know if the variable names and indentation match our Prettier config.
evals.expected_output: Focuses the review on correctness, design, and consistency rather than formatter-enforced style, noting that Prettier/lint already handles indentation. Still surfaces any real naming problems that affect readability, with line references and fixes.
